description: We are a multidisciplinary team passionate about Space Technology, Earth Observation, and Data Analytics. Our skills include Data Analysis, Programming, AI/ML, Web Development, and Storytelling. Through the MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge, we aim to harmonize satellite data and develop innovative solutions for accurate wildfire monitoring and detection. Our mission is to transform space data into real-world impact and protect our planet.
summary:
SpectraLink is an AI-powered Earth Observation platform and interactive 3D digital twin developed to solve the critical data discontinuity between NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite active fire records.

In 2012, Earth observation transitioned from 1,000m MODIS (Terra/Aqua) to 375m VIIRS (Suomi-NPP), causing an artificial ~4.04x spike in detected fire hotspots due to differing pixel resolutions and sensor geometries. Uncalibrated, researchers and policymakers risk mistaking this technological upgrade for an unprecedented climate disaster.

SpectraLink resolves this challenge using a physics-informed 32-feature geospatial pipeline coupled with SpectraNet Hybrid Stacking—an advanced machine learning ensemble achieving an R² of 0.987. It seamlessly harmonizes 25 years (2001–2025) of continuous fire records across ~200 countries, eliminating sensor transition gaps.

Beyond harmonization, SpectraLink applies Seiler & Crutzen combustion equations to quantify atmospheric CO₂ and PM₂.₅ smoke aerosol loads, provides 25-year seasonal climatology heatmaps, and delivers 6-month predictive forecasts. SpectraLink transforms raw orbital telemetry into an authoritative, actionable climate intelligence baseline for global wildfire mitigation.
details:
Overview: Solving Earth’s 25-Year Wildfire Observation Trap

Since 2000, NASA’s MODIS sensors aboard Terra and Aqua have monitored planetary thermal anomalies at 1,000 m resolution. In January 2012, NASA deployed the VIIRS sensor aboard Suomi-NPP (and later NOAA-20/21) at 375 m resolution. Because VIIRS has a 7.1× smaller pixel area, it detects smaller, lower-intensity agricultural and smoldering fires previously diluted below MODIS thresholds. This created an artificial +404% step-jump in raw fire detections. Without sensor harmonization, climate scientists, policymakers, and media risk mistaking a technological sensor upgrade for a sudden planetary wildfire crisis.

SpectraLink solves this critical challenge by building a physics-informed AI harmonization engine that unifies 25 years (2001–2025) of NASA MODIS and VIIRS satellite records across ~200 countries and diverse biomes into an authoritative, continuous baseline.

How It Works: Physics-Informed SpectraNet Architecture

Rather than treating fire counts as naive statistical numbers, SpectraLink models the complete physical transmission chain:

1. Orbital & Sensor Geometry: Corrects off-nadir pixel footprint expansion (A_pix = p₀ · sec²(θ_z)) and the bow-tie effect across orbital scan angles.

2. Atmospheric Radiative Transfer: Accounts for mid-infrared transmission attenuation (τ_MIR = exp(-m · AOD₅₅₀)) and total column water vapor using MOD04/MYD04 atmospheric products.

3. Dynamic Fuel & Biome Phenology: Extracts real-time vegetative moisture stress (NDWI) and greenness (NDVI/EVI) from MOD09GA surface reflectance alongside MCD12Q1 land cover taxonomy via Google Earth Engine.

4. Diurnal Progression: Calibrates 10:30 AM (Terra) morning passes with 1:30 PM (Aqua & VIIRS) afternoon peaks using Gaussian diurnal burning kernels.

5. SpectraNet Hybrid Stacking Ensemble: Blends gradient-boosted decision trees (LightGBM/XGBoost) with Huber-loss robust neural networks (δ = 1.35), achieving a 98.7% cross-sensor calibration accuracy (R² = 0.987) with a 74% RMSE error reduction.

Benefits & Real-World Impact

- Eliminating False Climate Trends: Restores an unbroken, calibrated 25-year historical record for UNFCCC and IPCC environmental reporting.

- Atmospheric Emission Quantifier: Directly computes total carbon release (CO₂, CO, CH₄) and fine respirable aerosol particulates (PM₂.₅) using Seiler & Crutzen combustion physics.

- 6-Month Predictive Horizon: Delivers regional seasonal fire forecasts with 95% confidence intervals, providing crucial early warning for disaster management authorities.

- Democratized Earth Science: Fully open-source and browser-based, enabling environmental agencies in developing nations to download calibrated regional fire datasets for free.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

- Languages & Backend: Python 3, FastAPI, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, Uvicorn.

- Geospatial & Planetary Processing: Google Earth Engine (GEE Python API), NASA FIRMS REST API, NASA Earthdata LAADS/LP-DAAC.

- Frontend & Visualization: Three.js (WebGL 3D celestial twin with real-time orbital ephemeris and swath cones), Leaflet.js (GIS raster heatmaps and cluster markers), Chart.js, HTML5/CSS3.

- Deployment: GitHub Pages (Static WebGL Client), Open-Source GitHub Repository.

Creativity & Key Engineering Considerations

- Dual-Stage Interactive Mission Control: Users experience a celestial 3D WebGL orbital Earth tracking Terra, Aqua, and VIIRS satellites in real time, with seamless one-click drill-down into any country's 25-year fire regime.

- Physical Fidelity: Prioritized robust Huber loss over standard MSE to prevent over-prediction on extreme mega-fires while preserving sensitivity to small agricultural burns.

- Zero-Latency In-Browser Experience: Pre-computed high-resolution vector matrices and client-side shaders ensure smooth 60 FPS performance even on low-bandwidth mobile devices.
